answers.question: Has Omar built design systems at scale?
aliases: has he built a design system
answers.answer:
Yes — four, and he treats them as infrastructure for a team rather than a personal artifact.

Athena Design System 2.0 at Plastiq is the deepest. He co-led it, audited every product to find where nomenclature and patterns had diverged, then ran workshops to align product, design and engineering on principles and KPIs before producing a single asset. He partnered with engineering on the Storybook implementation, and it became the foundation for Plastiq's IPO-era brand.

He built Wisdom's system from scratch as founding designer, rebuilt the one at Welcome Lend, and the fourth runs this portfolio and is published at /design-system. Earlier, at Disney, he and engineering started an ad-sales system — documentation and React components — and handed the foundation on.

answers.question: What's Omar's fintech and payments experience?
answers.answer:
Two years at Plastiq, 2021 to 2023, as Product Design Lead — 0→1 on a regulated product.

Plastiq Connect is an embedded payments product: a partner puts card and bank payments inside their own platform, under their own brand, and Plastiq carries the compliance and the disbursement. Benchmarking against Stripe Connect settled what it competed on — not feature breadth, but letting a partner hand PCI scope and risk operations over rather than build and certify them.

Compliance is visible in the design: masked stored cards, the encryption notice at the card-block boundary, beneficial-owner collection in the payer form, and a Texas step that fires on the payer's billing address.

$20M+ monthly volume in month one, three pre-launch partnerships, eight weeks signed to live.

answers.question: What AI or LLM work has Omar actually shipped?
answers.answer:
Two products at Wisdom, both designed so the model assists rather than decides.

Posting Assistant handles insurance payment posting. OCR and LLMs pull data out of scanned documents and surface it in a structured review interface, but specialists keep the judgment calls. He chose the assistive path over full automation deliberately, to preserve specialist trust. It cut manual posting time by about 40%.

Management Portal includes an LLM-powered Office Watchlist that flags offices when A/R aging crosses thresholds — over-60 and over-90 balances, week-over-week spikes — and explains what changed rather than just reporting that a rule fired. Its outcome metrics are projected rather than measured.

answers.question: Is Omar a design leader or an individual contributor?

He was the founding and sole design lead at Wisdom for two years, owning design across Management Portal, Reporting, Insurance Verification and Posting Assistant. At Plastiq he co-led the Athena design system and ran the cross-functional workshops that set its principles. On Disney's Unified Ad Platform he led two designers and mentored others on the wider design team.

He has stayed hands-on throughout, describing his current engagements as equal parts consulting and building — as likely to be rebuilding a design system as shipping a feature to production.

That number shaped what got built. The work ran through affinity mapping, journey maps, MoSCoW prioritisation and usability testing.

Across his career he puts the interview count at 500+, including 200+ at Wisdom.

answers.question: Tell me about the Wisdom Management Portal
answers.answer:
Wisdom's ops team was running 260+ dental offices across 9 Team Leads on 200+ interconnected Google Sheets. Risk stayed invisible until it became a crisis — at-risk clients surfaced too late and capacity was opaque.

He designed a centralised command centre around an LLM-powered Office Watchlist that evaluates A/R aging signals and ranks offices by urgency, plus workforce and capacity views. The watchlist explains what changed and why it tripped, rather than just firing a rule.

Its headline numbers — 200+ spreadsheets retired, scale from 260 to 900+ offices, 90%+ weekly active usage — are projected targets the design was built for, not measured results.

answers.question: Tell me about Posting Assistant
answers.answer:
Insurance payment posting at Wisdom was chaotic: documents arrived in every format, specialists jumped between screens comparing EOBs, and every posting needed a judgment call.

Rather than automate it outright, he designed an assistive workflow. OCR and LLMs extract the key data from scanned documents and present it in a structured review interface, with the specialist still deciding. He ran observational research with OBS Studio to capture how specialists actually worked across multiple monitors, plus 40+ interviews for this product specifically.

Result: about 40% less manual posting time, and a foundation for fuller automation later.

answers.question: Tell me about Plastiq Connect
answers.answer:
Plastiq Connect let a company put card and bank payments inside its own product, under its own brand. A buyer could pay a vendor by card even where that vendor did not accept cards, and the vendor was paid the way it already got paid — wire, ACH or a posted check.

Two products came out of it: the payer-facing widget a partner embedded, and the portal their developers used to integrate it. He led design 0→1 on both.

Compliance shaped the screens rather than sitting beside them — stored cards shown masked, the encryption notice placed at the boundary of the card block, and a Texas step triggered by the payer's billing address.

$20M+ monthly volume in month one, three partnerships secured pre-launch, and eight weeks from signed to live.

answers.question: Tell me about the Athena Design System
answers.answer:
Plastiq's products had drifted: inconsistent components, duplicate work, engineering unable to pick up what design produced, and no governing process.

He co-led the design system effort. They audited every product holistically before building anything, then ran workshops to align product, design and engineering on principles and KPIs — deliberately doing the alignment work before producing assets. He partnered with engineering on a Storybook implementation and documented layout grid, dashboard components, the payment widget and feedback indicators.

Engineering pickup time for global components dropped, 3+ products standardised on it, and it became the foundation for Plastiq's IPO-era brand.

answers.question: Tell me about the Disney Critical Communication Tool
answers.answer:
In 2019 a fire in Italy disrupted Disney network coverage and the right people were never notified. The existing tool either missed stakeholders entirely or flooded them.

He led all UX solo across a large cross-functional team, designing a self-service subscription manager that was scalable — brands and tags addable without architecture changes. The work ran through interviews with the Support Center, affinity mapping, journey maps, MoSCoW prioritisation and usability testing, with two versions of the subscription manager scrapped and rebuilt.

1,600+ users, 200,000+ emails sent, 250 critical incidents covered. It's the deepest case study on the site.

answers.question: Tell me about the Disney Unified Ad Platform
answers.answer:
AdVisor was Disney's ad-sales platform, and when the project started it served ESPN and nobody else. ABC, Disney, Hulu, ABC News, Freeform, FX Networks and National Geographic each ran their own tooling, so booking across the portfolio meant working in unrelated systems.

The job was bringing those seven brands onto AdVisor without regressing the workflow ESPN depended on daily. He started by mapping the decision flow rather than the screens — a current-state map tracing how a single decision moved through sales, traffic, promo, legal, operations, research and accounting.

Eight brand perspectives aligned on a shared model, ESPN's baseline preserved, and reusable patterns that fed Disney's Adapt design system. He led two designers and mentored others on the wider team.

answers.question: Tell me about Page Builder 2.0
answers.answer:
Simplero's page builder was so limiting that users were writing custom CSS to work around it and threatening to move to competitors. It also blocked migration from other platforms, so it was actively driving churn.

He led the full rebuild from scratch in two months — user and expert interviews, competitive analysis, and the product requirements, since there was no PM and he owned that role. He worked directly with the Lead Engineer to ship fast.

Four core capabilities shipped, contributing to a 9% increase in sales.

answers.question: Tell me about the Plastiq marketing site
answers.answer:
Plastiq needed a full site overhaul in three to four weeks ahead of going public. The old site buried products in navigation and didn't communicate value to investors or target customers.

He took the creative lead role without being formally assigned it — building the visual language, brand direction and content strategy, and running workshops to align an eight-person cross-functional team across design, copy, marketing and engineering.

Delivered on the three-to-four week timeline and WCAG compliant at launch.

answers.answer:

Their questions are not a payer's: where the keys are, what is hitting the endpoint, which transaction broke. So API keys were capped and shown masked to their last four characters with the whole rotate-and-expire lifecycle designed, IP whitelisting accepted CIDR ranges and validated the offending row inline, and transaction search carried a per-transaction issue state distinct from an empty result. Sandbox and production were split in the navigation.

Eight weeks from signed to live was a design target, not a sales number.

He also writes React and HTML/CSS/JS, so handoff tends to be a conversation.

answers.question: How does Omar handle accessibility?
answers.answer:
He treats it as a design-system requirement rather than QA cleanup. The design system powering this site states that plainly: WCAG AA is the floor, and focus states, keyboard flows, contrast, touch targets and reduced motion are requirements rather than fixes.

In practice: the Plastiq marketing site shipped WCAG compliant at launch on a three-to-four week timeline, and the Disney Critical Communication Tool carried accessibility as an explicit tag alongside mobile-first and scalable.

On this site every moving treatment has a stable equivalent under reduced motion, and that behaviour is enforced by automated browser tests.

When a question falls outside that set, a model drafts a reply from the closest reviewed answers, and that reply is labelled “drafted, not reviewed” wherever it appears. The label is the point: reviewed and drafted are never presented as the same thing.

On a hiring site, an assistant that quietly invents a detail is worse than one that flags what has not been checked. For anything that matters, email him.

answers.question: What data does this assistant collect?

Questions that match a written answer are answered in your browser from the static corpus. When nothing matches, the question is sent to Groq with excerpts from the closest published answers so it can draft a reply.

If you accepted analytics, the wording of the question is recorded in an analytics event so Omar can see which answers are missing. If you declined, it isn't recorded.

The full picture is in the privacy policy, linked in the footer.

answers.question: What kinds of problems should a team bring Omar in to solve?

The work is most useful where a team needs senior design judgement and hands-on execution at the same time — someone who will map the decision flow before drawing screens, and then draw the screens. On the Disney Unified Ad Platform that meant tracing how one decision moved through seven business functions before any interface existed.

It is a poor fit for work that is already well defined and only needs producing.
